surfaces.part: book rows on three shelves (goods on shelves)

answer.evidence: Rows 1-6 form a pale top band, 6 rows deep, with a slightly darker front-edge line at row 6 (L=204 against 242 above). Row 7 is a dark band (L=45) directly below it and acts as eave shadow. Below that, the front face runs from row 7 to row 30, about 24 rows. It shows the shelf interior with books, white shelf-board lines at rows 13, 20 and 27, and a wooden base at row 28. The top band is thicker than a 1-2 row rim and matches the green 'cabinet: top 5 + edge + eave' reference. No side face is drawn. The silhouette is a constant 30 px wide.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's visible-tone count (20 per tile) matches the well and cheese stall, and it has 0% near-flat coverage, so density is not the problem. But the 20 tones come mostly from the many book hues, not from shading depth. The white/grey frame and shelf boards show only about 3 lightness steps (white, light grey, grey), against 5-6 per material in the Beodeul references. The measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 100%, and the outline looks like a neutral grey-black line around the frame and books. That is the sticker look. The references with tinted outlines (hedge 0%, cheese 1%, well 33%) use dark material tones instead. The frame has no grain, speckle or wood texture, and the books are tiny, uniform colour blocks. Next to the cheese stall and well it reads cleaner and flatter. Verdict is fail on the neutral outline and shallow material shading, even though the tone count is high.

surfaces.part: shelf front with books and shelf boards

answer.evidence: Rows 1-6 form a light band at the top, with a lighter-edge outline at row 1. It ends in a slightly darker front-edge line at row 6 (L=204), and row 7 is a dark shadow (L=45) directly below it. That reads as a top surface about 6 rows tall. The front face runs from row 7 to row 29 and shows three shelf bays of colored books. White single-row shelf boards sit at rows 13, 20 and 27, and a wood base is at row 28. No side face is drawn. The drawing is a flat frontal view, but the top band with its edge line and shadow is enough evidence of a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts look fine on the surface: 20 visible tones per tile (the well reference also has 20, the cheese stall 17) and 0% near-flat coverage. Looking at the picture, most of those tones come from the many small, differently coloured book spines, not from shaded material ramps. The white/grey frame and shelf boards have only about 2-3 lightness steps (white, light grey, grey) and read as flat panels. The outline is a neutral dark grey line around the whole shelf, and 100% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral. References such as the hedge (0%), the cheese stall (1%) and the roofed well (33%) use dark material-tone edges instead, so the candidate has the uniform 'sticker' outline. It has no wood grain, no per-plank highlights and no material texture, and the books are simple uniform bars. Next to the stall and well, it looks flatter and more sticker-like.
